app: GNOME Chess — annotated-game boundary at the RENDER-TREE level (counterpart of macOS Chess via AX)
channel_setup: gdb tap on /usr/games/gnome-chess under broadway; frame re-rendered to PNG for verification.

t1_read_text.detail: Chrome text readable (3 nodes: 'White to Move', engine banner, 'Game Start').

t2_enumerate.detail: The BOARD renders as ~10 texture nodes (pieces/squares rasterized from SVG into textures) — no per-piece structure at the render level. Contrast with macOS Chess where the SEMANTIC channel (AX) exposed each piece as an annotated button. Two-part boundary confirmed: (a) which CHANNEL you read (semantic vs render), and (b) developer annotation. The render tree declares the board as textures (croppable, explicit), it does not fabricate structure. gnome-chess's AT-SPI annotations untestable headless (a11y bus blocked) — expected to be the semantic mirror, to verify on a real Linux desktop.

t6_pictorial.detail: Board textures are declared opaque payloads with rects — explicit, croppable; re-rendered PNG matches the app window exactly (artifact).

measurements.notes: Probe-hygiene lesson recorded on ourselves: first run captured STALE frames of widget-factory (gnome-chess lives in /usr/games, `which` failed silently, rm never ran) and the census looked plausible. Caught because we re-render every captured tree to pixels before believing it — runtime verification catching our own harness, again.

runtime_verification.agreement: exact (chess board with initial position, engine-missing banner)
